newsitem.title: VATICAN: Vatican report demands morality in advertising.
newsitem.headline: Vatican report demands morality in advertising.

text.p: The Vatican on Tuesday urged advertisers to stop pandering to lust, envy and greed and show more morality in their work.
A 30-page report on "Ethics in Advertising" prepared by the Vatican's Pontifical Council for Social Communications said advertisers had a moral duty to be truthful and to serve the common good.

While acknowledging that advertising could be socially useful, especially in market economies, the report criticised the industry for the way it depicted women, its influence over children and for the high cost of promoting politics.

And in particularly strong wording, the report attacked government-sponsored advertising of "artificial birth control... abortifacients...so-called 'safe sex' and similar practices", which are not allowed under Roman Catholic Church teachings.
It said this type of advertising encouraged "attitudes and forms of behaviour contrary to moral norms."

But the report added that if used well, advertising could inspire people. "Advertising has significant potential for good...(it) can brighten lives simply by being witty, tasteful and entertaining," it said.
Abuses came about when advertising was used to persuade or motivate people to act in a certain way.

"Advertising that reduces human progress to acquiring material goods and cultivating a lavish lifestyle expresses a false, destructive vision of the human person harmful to individuals and societies alike," it said.

The report, which will be distributed to advertising agengies, said manipulative devices "promoting consumeristic attitudes" were particularly damaging in developing countries. "The result is that they waste their resources, neglect their real needs and genuine development falls behind."
In further condemnation, the report said advertising could be "vulgar and morally degrading...Frequently it deliberately appeals to such motives as envy, status-seeking and lust".
It added that some advertising was designed to "shock and titillate by exploiting content of a morbid, perverse, pornographic nature".
The Vatican urged advertisers to regulate themselves "to ensure ethically responsible practices in their profession".
"Advertisers...are morally responsible for what they seek to move people to do," it said.
